input.summary: Identified three currently affiliated EMBL group leaders with defensible relevance to Priya’s computational single-cell host–pathogen goals, while separating research-fit evidence from PhD-recruitment evidence. Nassos Typas is the strongest overall match and is explicitly listed on EMBL’s current recruiting-group page.

sections.title: 1. Nassos Typas — strongest overall fit
sections.body: Current affiliation: Head of Molecular Systems Biology and group leader at EMBL Heidelberg; the official profile states he has been an EMBL group leader since 2011. Fit evidence: the Typas Group develops high-throughput quantitative/genome-wide approaches for bacterial cellular networks, microbial communities, and interactions with hosts; EMBL’s Infection Biology page specifically describes computational and experimental work on bacteria–host interactions. This aligns well with Priya’s pathogen genomics, reproducible computational workflows, and interest in host–pathogen biology, although the group’s public description is more systems-microbiology/genetics than explicitly scRNA-seq. Acceptance evidence: **yes, current recruitment evidence found**—Typas appears on EMBL’s current International PhD Programme recruiting-group page. citeturn1search0turn1search3turn1search6turn2view0

sections.title: 2. Maria Bernabeu Aznar — strongest pathogen/host biology fit
sections.body: Current affiliation: Group Leader and Co-chair of EMBL’s Infection Biology Transversal Theme at EMBL Barcelona. Fit evidence: her official group page focuses directly on *Plasmodium falciparum* cerebral malaria, host–parasite interactions, endothelial/brain-barrier responses, advanced imaging, and omics. This is especially relevant to Priya’s accepted first-author work on severe malaria and her single-cell host-response interests. The public page does not establish that the group routinely uses scRNA-seq, so the single-cell fit should be treated as a plausible bridge rather than a confirmed lab method. Acceptance evidence: **not verified** from the official sources reviewed; Bernabeu was not present on the current EIPP recruiting-group list retrieved on August 8, 2026. citeturn0search2turn0search8turn0search11turn2view0

sections.title: 3. Michael Zimmermann — computational/omics host–microbiome fit
sections.body: Current affiliation: Group Leader at EMBL Heidelberg since August 2019. Fit evidence: his group studies metabolic microbiome–host interactions using high-throughput mass spectrometry, bacterial genetics, culturing, bioinformatics, and functional microbiome sequencing; the group’s recent work includes multi-omics and host–microbiome biology. This fits Priya’s computational biology, pathogen/microbial genomics, and reproducible workflow background, but is less directly focused on pathogenic infection or single-cell transcriptomics than Typas or Bernabeu. Acceptance evidence: **yes, group-level PhD opportunity evidence found**—the official open-positions page explicitly says there are currently opportunities for PhD students and directs PhD applicants through the EMBL International PhD Programme. citeturn0search0turn0search1turn0search4

sections.title: Recruitment interpretation
sections.body: EMBL states that its recruiting-group page identifies groups actively looking to hire PhD students, but also warns that the list is preliminary and may change before interviews. Therefore, “listed on the recruiting page” is stronger evidence than a general group open-positions page, but neither guarantees an offer or a project match. citeturn2view0

follow_ups: Before naming supervisors in an application, recheck the EIPP recruiting list and each group’s open-positions page immediately before submission.
For a targeted enquiry, prioritize Typas first, Bernabeu second for malaria/host-response alignment, and Zimmermann third for microbiome/omics methodology.
